## Try It Yourself

::: {.callout-tip}
## How to Practice
1. **Run the code** to see multiple regression in action
2. **Compare R² values** across models to see the improvement
3. **Copy to RStudio** for your notebook exercises
:::

### Run Multiple Regression

```{webr-r}
# Predict wellbeing from three variables
model <- lm(wellbeing ~ stress + sleep_hours + exercise_mins,
            data = wellbeing)
summary(model)
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Key Output
Each coefficient shows the effect of that predictor **holding all others constant**.
Check both Adjusted R² and the F-statistic for overall model fit.
:::

### Compare Models

```{webr-r}
model1 <- lm(wellbeing ~ stress, data = wellbeing)
model2 <- lm(wellbeing ~ stress + sleep_hours, data = wellbeing)
model3 <- lm(wellbeing ~ stress + sleep_hours + exercise_mins,
             data = wellbeing)

cat("Model 1 (stress only):      R² =", round(summary(model1)$r.squared, 3), "\n")
cat("Model 2 (+ sleep):          R² =", round(summary(model2)$r.squared, 3), "\n")
cat("Model 3 (+ exercise):       R² =", round(summary(model3)$r.squared, 3), "\n\n")
cat("Adjusted R² for Model 3:   ", round(summary(model3)$adj.r.squared, 3))
```

### Standardised Coefficients

```{webr-r}
# Standardise variables to compare predictor importance
wellbeing_z <- data.frame(
  wellbeing = scale(wellbeing$wellbeing),
  stress    = scale(wellbeing$stress),
  sleep     = scale(wellbeing$sleep_hours),
  exercise  = scale(wellbeing$exercise_mins)
)

model_std <- lm(wellbeing ~ stress + sleep + exercise, data = wellbeing_z)
betas <- round(coef(model_std)[-1], 3)

cat("Standardised coefficients (β):\n")
cat("  Stress:   β =", betas["stress"], "\n")
cat("  Sleep:    β =", betas["sleep"], "\n")
cat("  Exercise: β =", betas["exercise"], "\n\n")
cat("Larger |β| = stronger predictor (all in same SD units)")
```
